Steno- means narrow and -haline refers to salinity, so stenohaline organisms tolerate only a narrow range of salinity. Euryhaline organisms tolerate a wide range.

Organisms that can tolerate a wide range of temperature are termed:
'Eury-' means wide and '-thermal' relates to temperature, so eurythermal organisms can tolerate a wide range of temperature.
Salinity of ocean water is expressed in units of:
The salt concentration of water is measured as salinity, expressed in parts per thousand (ppt).
The dependence of flowering in many plants on the relative lengths of day and night is called:
Many plants depend on the duration of light for their flowering; this response is called photoperiodism.
The maintenance of a constant internal environment by an organism is called:
All organisms try to maintain a constant internal environment in order to sustain maximum functionality; this maintenance is called homeostasis.

A thick cuticle on the leaf surface of desert plants primarily checks:
A thick cuticle on the leaf surface checks transpiration, helping desert plants conserve water.

A declining population is represented by an age pyramid of which shape?
A declining population gives an urn-shaped age pyramid, where the pre-reproductive base is narrower than the reproductive middle.
For grass or lichens covering the ground, population density is best expressed as:
Population density may be expressed as per cent cover for species such as grass or lichens, where counting individuals is impractical.
Birth rate is also referred to as:
Birth rate is also called natality -- the number of live births per one thousand individuals per year.
All the rats living in an abandoned dwelling, capable of interbreeding, together constitute:
All the rats in an abandoned dwelling, being similar individuals capable of interbreeding in a shared geographical area, together constitute a population.
If, over a given period, (B + I) is less than (D + E), the population will:
If (B + I) < (D + E), the population declines because more individuals are lost than added.
In dN/dt = (b - d) × N, the term (b - d) is substituted with the symbol:
Substituting (b - d) = r gives the standard form dN/dt = rN, where r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase.
The exponential growth curve, when population size is plotted against time, is described as:
Plotted against time, exponential growth gives an unbounded J-shaped curve.
When N is much smaller than K, the term (K - N)/K in the logistic equation is close to:
When N is small compared to K, (K-N)/K is close to 1, and growth is nearly exponential.
Populations tend to increase their reproductive fitness, a concept referred to in ecology as:
Populations tend to increase their reproductive fitness so as to survive better -- this is called Darwinian fitness, reflected in a high r value.
Lice on humans and ticks on dogs are examples of:
Ectoparasites live outside the body of the host. Examples: lice on humans, ticks on dogs, and ectoparasitic copepods on marine fish.
Plasmodium, liver fluke, tapeworm and roundworm are all examples of:
Endoparasites live inside the body of the host; examples include Plasmodium, liver fluke, tapeworm and roundworm.
In the mycorrhizal association, the plant provides the fungi with:
In mycorrhizae, the fungi help the plant absorb nutrients from the soil, while the plant provides the fungi with energy-yielding carbohydrates.
In the fig-wasp mutualism, the female wasp uses the fig fruit chiefly as a site for:
The female wasp uses the fig fruit as an oviposition (egg-laying) site and uses the developing seeds within it to nourish her larvae, pollinating the fig in the process.
The Ophrys-bee relationship is considered a classic example of:
The Ophrys-bee relationship is a plant-pollinator mutualism and a classic example of co-evolution, where both species have evolved together.
Amensalism is described in this chapter as the mirror image of:
Amensalism is the mirror image of commensalism: in commensalism one gains and the other is neutral; in amensalism one loses and the other is neutral.
A population's sex ratio, age distribution and density together are called its:
Sex ratio, age distribution, density, natality and mortality are together called the attributes of a population.
A camouflaged insect that resembles a dry leaf is best understood as a defence against:
Camouflage such as resembling a dry leaf helps prey animals avoid detection by predators, and is thus a defence against predation.
A cheetah chasing and killing a gazelle for food is a direct example of:
A cheetah killing and consuming a gazelle is a direct example of predation, a (+,-) interaction where the predator benefits and the prey is harmed.

A fish that can survive only within a narrow temperature range of 24–26°C is best described as:
Organisms restricted to a narrow range of temperature are called stenothermal (steno = narrow, thermal = temperature).
An organism capable of tolerating a very wide range of environmental temperatures is called:
Organisms that can tolerate a wide range of temperature are called eurythermal (eury = wide, thermal = temperature).
The salt concentration of water, known as salinity, is expressed in units of:
The salt concentration of water is measured as salinity, expressed in parts per thousand (ppt).
The dependence of flowering in many plants on the duration of light they receive is called:
Many plants depend on the duration of light for their flowering; this response is called photoperiodism.
When conditions become stressful, an organism may adopt one of how many broad strategies?
When conditions become stressful, an organism may adopt one of four strategies: Regulate, Conform, Migrate or Suspend.
On a graph of internal level versus external level, a regulator is represented by:
On a graph of internal level versus external level, conformers give a rising straight line, while regulators give a flat horizontal line.
Bacteria and lower plants tide over unfavourable conditions mainly by forming:
Spores are formed in bacteria and lower plants to tide over unfavourable conditions.
Zooplankton entering a stage of suspended development during unfavourable conditions is called:
Diapause is the stage of suspended development that zooplankton enter during unfavourable conditions.
Population size, more technically, is referred to as:
Population size, more technically, is referred to as population density (N), which indicates the number of individuals inhabiting a particular niche.
The population density of grass or lichens covering an area is most appropriately expressed as:
Population density, depending on the species, may be expressed as per cent cover, as for grass or lichens.
In a population, if (B + I) is greater than (D + E) over a given period, the population:
If (B + I) > (D + E), the population grows; if (B + I) < (D + E), it declines; if they are equal, the population is stable.
Interactions between two different species of organisms in a habitat are called:
Interspecific interactions are interactions between two different species of organisms; they may be beneficial or harmful to one or both partners.
Parasites that live outside the body of their host are called:
Ectoparasites live outside the body of the host; examples include lice on humans and ticks on dogs.
Parasites that live inside the body of their host, such as Plasmodium and tapeworm, are called:
Endoparasites live inside the body of the host; examples include Plasmodium, liver fluke, tapeworm and roundworm.
The Ophrys orchid and bee relationship is cited in this chapter as a classic example of:
The Ophrys orchid and bee relationship, involving sexual deceit for pollination, is a classic example of co-evolution.
Ectoparasitic copepods that infest many marine fish are an example of:
Ectoparasitic copepods that infest many marine fish are listed as ectoparasites, living outside the body of the host.
